intended_object: An ad hoc helper function for a proof: the real function (a, δ, v) ↦ correctionRoot δ v / √a. It is the square root of the variance correction that is fed into `solvedTilt` when the seed tilt of the parametric modulation construction is built. I inferred this from the docstring and from how the library uses it.
explanation: The definition is a single-line formula used inside the library's Navier–Stokes cone-loop construction. It combines other local helpers: `correctionRoot δ v = speedCutoff δ v * √(targetSpeed δ − v)`. The lemmas proved about it are nonnegativity, `varianceRoot^2 = correction/a`, vanishing at high speed and a bound. They all serve the next step, which plugs it into `solvedTilt` to set the variance of the seed tilt. No standard mathematical notion corresponds to it, so it has no Mathlib counterpart and no natural generality to compare against. It is an internal device for the proof.
